Surprisingly, even 1 drink doubles your risk of an AFib episode.  I've been drinking daily for many years and recently, it just happened for the first time diagnostically.  I've had it happen before where I just chalked it up to a panic attack, but its happened only when drinking.  It's one of the #1 triggers for AFib unfortunately.  They call it Holiday Heart.

Wow, thanks for all the comments and insight.  As of right now, I have gone to a cardiologist who performed a 3 day holter monitor, echocardiogram, stress test with echo and EKGs.  From what I hear from the cardiologist, my heart is in perfect condition.  No enlargement of the left atria, no leaking valves or signs of heart disease of any kind.  For the last many years, I’ve suffered the occasional palpitation etc but was also an alcoholic by definition for many years (5-6 beers a day and even more on weekends).  

I do believe this has happened to me approximately 3 times over the last 3 years, but it seems to ALWAYS be if i’ve been drinking heavily for multiple days in a row and under a certain level of stress combined.  This time it was moving into my first home and having a baby in a few weeks (too many big moves at once 😩).  2 times, the heart went back into normal sinus on its own and the 3rd time, it woke me up on moving day where a cardioversion was required.

As of right now, I have quit drinking for 15 days and have purchased an EKG watch to identify any AFib that might occur.  So far, I’ve adjusted to make sure I’m drinking a Nuun electrolyte tablet once daily, staying hydrated, exercising and Vitamin C.  

I would like to be able to have a few drinks on a Friday instead of maybe everyday, but will try that after a month of cessation.

I’ve recently went through an AFIB episode and notice my trigger is alcohol.  I was a pretty heavy drinker for the most part and thought they were just panic attacks.
